 Cummins India Reports 4% Revenue Growth in Q2 FY27
 MM Desk 
 05/11/2026 
 Share 
 Image Courtesy: Cummins India 
 Cummins India Limited reported standalone total sales of ₹3,247 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, an increase of 4% over the corresponding quarter of the previous year. Sales declined 4% compared with the preceding quarter. Domestic sales stood at ₹2,692 crore, registering year-on-year growth of 5%, while declining 6% sequentially. Export sales increased 2% year-on-year and 6% quarter-on-quarter to ₹555 crore.
 Profit before tax (PBT) for the quarter was ₹601 crore, representing a decline of 28.4% from the same quarter last year and 16.6% from the previous quarter. The company reported profit after tax (PAT) of ₹467 crore, with a net profit margin of 14.4%. PBT margin stood at 18.5%. The Board of Directors reviewed and approved the unaudited financial results for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, at its meeting held in November.
 Adegbile Adewunmi, Managing Director, Cummins India Limited, said demand remained healthy across key domestic markets, supported by data centres, manufacturing, real estate and growth in the distribution business. Export sales also increased compared with the previous quarter.
 He said commodity and freight cost inflation, along with changes in product mix, affected margins during the quarter. The benefits of pricing measures are expected to become visible progressively. The company will continue to focus on order execution, price realisation and cost management.
 Looking ahead, Cummins India expects demand across its key domestic and export markets to remain steady. However, geopolitical uncertainty, inflation, commodity price movements and changing supply-chain conditions continue to influence the operating environment. The company said it would maintain its focus on operational efficiency, disciplined execution and prudent capital deployment. Its balance sheet and cash conversion cycle provide support for continued investment while managing costs.
 Established in 1962 and headquartered in Pune, Cummins India is part of the Cummins Group and operates in power generation, aftermarket services and exports. The company has four manufacturing plants, along with assembly operations and a distribution centre. Its products and services are supported by a network of around 480 customer touchpoints across India. The company employs more than 3,000 people and provides power solutions and related services to customers across various industries.
